summary: D. Dennis Hudson was a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He earned his Ph.D. from Claremont Graduate University around 1964–1970 and served as a professor in the Department of Religion and Biblical Studies at Smith College from 1970 to 2000.

D. H. Gordon worked in the fields of Indology and history and archaeology. He was educated at Wellington College from around 1909 to 1913 and at the Royal Military Academy Sandhurst between roughly 1913 and 1914.

D. L. Narasimhachar was an Indology and linguistics scholar. After studying at Maharaja's College, Mysore (c. 1925–1929), he held a post at the University of Mysore from around 1932 to 1962 and taught T. V. Venkatachala Sastry.

D. N. Dimri worked in Indology and history and archaeology. Educated as a doctoral researcher at Doon University (2014), he held positions at WWF-India, UEEC, the Archaeological Survey of India (attested 2016), and the University of Pannonia (2018–2019).

D. N. Shukla was an Indologist who completed a D.Litt. at the University of Lucknow under the doctoral supervision of K. A. Subramania Iyer. He was affiliated with Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gorakhpur University in 1958.

D. Neil Schmid is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at Waseda University, the École Pratique des Hautes Études, and the University of Pennsylvania, where he completed his doctoral studies under Victor H. Mair.

D. R. Nagaraj was an Indologist. He completed his studies at Bangalore University around 1971–1977, taught Sheldon Pollock, and served on the faculty at Bangalore University from approximately 1978 until 1998.
D. S. Subbaramaiya was a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He pursued his traditional education under Mallikere Subrahmanya Sastri and V. S. Ramachandra Sastri.
D. Srinivasachar was an Indologist. In the years 1931–1933, he was attested as Professor of Sanskrit at Maharaja's College, Mysore, and as Curator at the Oriental Research Institute Mysore.

Dagfinn Føllesdal studied at the University of Oslo and Harvard University under W. V. O. Quine. Working in philosophy and linguistics, he taught at Harvard, held professorships at the University of Oslo and Stanford University, and taught Bimal Krishna Matilal.

Dagmar Schwerk is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned her degrees, including a PhD under Dorji Wangchuk, at the University of Hamburg. She held fellowships at the University of British Columbia and became a professor at Leipzig in 2024.

Dagmar Wujastyk works in the fields of Indology and history and archaeology. She served as Principal Investigator at the University of Vienna in 2015 and became an Associate Professor at the University of Alberta in 2018.

Dagpo Rinpoche is a figure in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under the 14th Dalai Lama, Ngawang Nyima, Thubten Lungtog Tenzin Trinley, and Trijang Rinpoche, and taught David Seyfort Ruegg, Anne-Marie Blondeau, Thoupten Phuntshog, and Marie-Stella Boussemart.

Taichi Tado works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He has held teaching posts at Waseda University (attested 2020), the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (attested 2020–2026), and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

Daiei Kaneko was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Otani University and under Manshi Kiyozawa. He founded Koho Gakuen and held academic appointments at Toyo University (c. 1916–1928) and Otani University (c. 1925–1928).
Daigo Sasaki is a Buddhist studies researcher who is attested in 2006 as a research student (kenkyūsei) at Ryukoku University.

Daijaku Judith Kinst works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. She served as a faculty member at the Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 2013) and as Professor Emerita at the Numata Center for Buddhist Translation and Research (attested 2026).
Daiju Sasaki is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Taisho University (c. 1996–2005). He held teaching roles at Taisho University (attested 2015, c. 2018) and at Chisan Denpōin (attested 2015).

Daijō Tokiwa was a Buddhist studies and Sinology scholar educated at the University of Tokyo under Tetsujiro Inoue and Yujiro Motora. He taught at Tokyo and Toyo University, served at the Academy of Oriental Culture, and taught Enichi Ocho.

Dainin Katagiri was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Komazawa University, Eihei-ji, and under Eko Hashimoto and Daicho Hayashi. He served at Zenshuji Soto Mission and San Francisco Zen Center, and founded the Minnesota Zen Meditation Center.
